verdict.rationale: Community advocates say GitLab has an open-source core that anyone can run or fork. First-party docs support source access only indirectly: they describe self-compiling GitLab and point to the raw OpenAPI spec in the GitLab monorepo. Missing for 10: first-party documentation naming the open-source license (e.g., MIT) and its scope across editions, a documented public source repository location, and clarity on which features are open versus proprietary.
